elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall not pay Vendor any liquidated damages or penalty"
"any liquidated damages or penalty, including any amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees"

elements.element: Direction: obligation runs from Customer to Vendor (Customer-payable amounts eliminated)
elements.evidence: "Customer shall not pay Vendor" replaces "Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty"

elements.element: Any liquidated amount limited to an early-termination fee
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee exists; clause now bars "any liquidated damages or penalty" — condition demonstrably absent

elements.element: Cap of 3 months' fees on that fee
elements.evidence: No liquidated amount survives to be capped: "shall not pay Vendor any liquidated damages or penalty"

elements.element: Such fee is the sole liquidated amount
elements.evidence: Blanket prohibition leaves no other liquidated amount: "including any amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week"

reasons: The single replacement negates the payment operator ('shall pay' → 'shall not pay ... any liquidated damages or penalty'), which fully achieves the preferred position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer.

The retained trailing description ('including any amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid') is original text repurposed as an illustrative exclusion, not new substantive language, so the edit remains a minimal operator flip rather than a clause rewrite.
Payment timing, the ten-day trigger and Vendor's other remedies (e.g., interest, suspension, termination) are untouched; no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
Fallback elements are inapplicable because no early-termination fee is created or preserved; the blanket prohibition is at least as protective.
